chunks: As for what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub has narrated — from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (AS) — he said:
'The kurr of water is approximately like this jar of mine,' and he pointed to a jar from those jars that are found in Medina.
So it is not impossible that the jar holds the measure of a kurr of water, and this is not far-fetched.

key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: our companions: standard formula in Shia isnads for unnamed but trusted Shia transmitters, making this chain technically mursal
key_terms.الْحُبُّ: a large clay storage jar (pl. al-hibab), commonly used in Medina for storing water or foodstuffs
key_terms.الْكُرُّ: the kurr: a unit of volume in Shia fiqh (~384 liters / ~1200 ritls) above which water cannot be rendered impure by najasah
key_terms.مِقْدَارَ: the measure, quantity, specified amount of

ai.seo_question: What is the kurr measure of water according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) defines the kurr — the minimum volume of water that cannot be rendered ritually impure by contact with najasah — by gesturing to a large clay storage jar (hubb) commonly used in Medina. Shaykh al-Tusi appends his own jurisprudential note affirming that it is plausible for such a jar to contain a full kurr of water.
